questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study animals and ecology in a place very different from my own home in Denmark. I did exchange to study subjects that where not available to me at copenhagen university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really good. Monash university sent a lot of email out with what i need to do and there was also a pre arrival zoom meeting. only thing that could be better would be one big email instead of all the small ones

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a big meeting/mixer with all the exchange student where the told us all from how to get to class, to aussie slang. I was living on campus so i had a lot of additional orientation which was great

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: there were classic dorms where you had a room and shared bathroom, kitchen and commen area with fellow students (i had that one). There where small one room apartments with own kitchen and bathroom. And then there where small multiple room shared apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: i dont know about meal plans but there was a nice cheap dorm cafe. And the university handed out a surprising ammount of free food. Cooking facilities where one big kitchen shared by 20-30 people. It was a lotteri, some kitchen where gross because of the people and other were great. I liked mine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its cheaper then most places in the city. You save a lot of public transport because you walk to class. It was the best decision i made. I got a lot of friends from australia and all over the world (other exchange students). Campus is however an hour outside the city so you wont be living in down town melbourne

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky to get on campus house. A lot were not

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to find where it is on the website but after that it was easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you log into a portal and then select the courses. a lot like KU

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: they were very kind over email. but other than that i didnt need help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: start early and have a few backups. but other than that its quite straight forward

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i did third year bachelor courses which fit with my own level. i liked them, some had a lot of stuff i already learned in cph but a lot other stuff was completly new.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: they take roll call so you have to show up. A lot more emphasis on the assignment than on the final exam. very different than KU

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Animal Behavior
Biology of Australian vertebrates
Conservation biology
Advanced methods in field ecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
animal behavior is like a trail for writing a small bachelor project. you get to design an experiment and complete it during the semester. 
Advanced methods in fields ecology teaches you to do research. it was really good and helped shape you understadning of science, it also teaches you to read and under other littiture

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The visa is REALLY GOD DAMN expensive!!!!!!!!!!!! it was 3000 dkk when i got it but has now gone up to 7000dkk as i am writing this !!!!!!!!!!!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: meet and public transport is cheaper. Some vegetables is very expensive but overall it was pretty much the same

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot! surf camps, hiking clubs, event nights. it was great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a big sports center with fitness and swimming. our dorm had netball tornements. there were a lot of tours you could go on through dorm, all from histpry to city exploration to sancturaies. (and they were affordable too)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: if you get into any of the dorm, go on the trips!!! they are great and you get a lot of value for money. If you like it, i heard surf camp was a really reallly fun thing to go on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
go to tasmania! rent a car and drive around, if you go with a group its cheap. Go to phillip island and wilson prompt. If when you have time, do east coast!!! great barrier reef is incredable. Magnetic island on east coast is gret too. 
40 from clayton campus moonlit sancturay lies and here you can feed kangaroos and wallabies!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy. the slang and accent takes a bit of getting used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to all the events in the beginning, even if youre tired. it is so fun

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the kindness. everyone was so kind and out going

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: be aware which campus your classes are on as there are 2. but there is a free shuttle bus between them that goes all day but it takes at least 30 minutes

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the people and the animals. i got so many great friends and learned a lot about other cultures. the animal experiances where amazing too, both in my studies and the my free time. if you study biology it is really a great place to go.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: homesickness. Australia is far away and expensive to fly to. i only had one friend who could afford to visit me. so just aware of that but time flies by fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
